newsitem.title: PERU: Peru lifts ban on family visits to jailed rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru lifts ban on family visits to jailed rebels.

text.p: Peru has lifted a ban on family visits to jailed leftist Tupac Amaru guerrillas imposed during the group's armed seizure of the Japanese ambassador's home, prison officials said on Monday.
But it has not allowed the resumption of International Red Cross visits to imprisoned Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) members, a National Penitentiary Institute official told Reuters.

In December, the government stopped the monthly, half-hour family visits granted to jailed MRTA members, after guerrillas took hundreds of VIPs hostage at the diplomatic residence to demand the release of over 400 comrades in Peru's jails.

Almost two months after Peruvian troops crushed the siege and killed the 14 hostage-takers, the lifting of the ban was welcome news to relatives, who supplement the prisoners' poor diet by taking food into the jails.

"Terrific," Rhoda Berenson, mother of Lori Berenson, an American woman jailed for life for belonging to the MRTA, said by telephone from New York. "We'll be down as quickly as possible and every month after that."
